question: arXiv:2610.26648v1 quotes a J-factor integrated over its Galactic Center fitting region, while Elor, Rodd and Slatyer, in their paper on multi-step cascade annihilations of dark matter and the Galactic Center excess, quote a J-factor averaged over their region of interest. Give both values together with the region each refers to and the solid angle of the fitting region of arXiv:2610.26648v1, and say whether the two values agree once they are put on the same footing.

arguments.query: multi-step cascade annihilations dark matter Galactic Center excess
arguments.author: Slatyer

first_line.asked: query='multi-step cascade annihilations dark matter Galactic Center excess' author='Slatyer'

arguments.answer: arXiv:2610.26648v1 quotes an integrated J_ann = 8.86×10^22 GeV^2 cm^-5 over its GC fitting region, the 40°×40° square with |b|>2° (ΔΩ = 0.429 sr). Elor, Rodd & Slatyer (arXiv:1503.01773) quote an ROI-averaged J_norm ≈ 2.0618×10^23 GeV^2 cm^-5 over |l|≤20°, 2°≤|b|≤20°. This is the same region and the same NFW profile (γ=1.2, r_s=20 kpc, ρ(r_sun)=0.4 GeV/cm^3, r_sun=8.5 kpc). Using ΔΩ = 0.6981 rad × 2(sin20°−sin2°) ≈ 0.429 sr (my arithmetic), 2.0618×10^23 × 0.429 ≈ 8.84×10^22, versus 8.86×10^22 (equivalently 8.86×10^22/0.429 ≈ 2.07×10^23 as an average). So the two values agree to about 0.2%; the apparent factor ~2.3×10^0 difference is only integrated versus averaged.
